text:
maya: heads-up — saw other org rows flash into an Insights panel when I switched workspaces rapidly in prod. screenshot: https://redwood-internal/ps/IMG_8812.png

jamal: yikes. steps to repro? browser/flags?

maya: repro steps: 1) open org A -> open Insights panel (stable) 2) quick-switch to org B (top-right) 3) immediately click Refresh on panel. For ~150-250ms some rows from A render, then corrected. Happened on Chrome + Firefox, prod only (no canary).

zane: can repro locally with a high-speed session. looks like a prefetch race: prefetch service serving cached snapshot before request finishes routing/namespace binding.

anika: do we have any logs showing the prefetch key composition? last time similar bug the cache key omitted org id.

zane: pulling logs — here's the relevant snippet from prefetch service (typescript):

```js
// current code in master (bad)
const cacheKey = `prefetch:${route}:${userId}`;
// missing orgId -> collisions when routing header delayed

// proposed fix:
const cacheKey = `prefetch:${route}:${orgId}:${userId}`;
```

jamal: if headers propagate slowly between edge->router->prefetch, the service may read a request without X-Org set and serve a stale entry. That matches the 150ms flash.

leo: we also saw telemetry traces with mismatched org_id earlier this week (anika raised it). Could be the same causality chain: internal API forwards accidentally drop the namespace header for some fast path.

anika: confirmed — our internal gateway has a fast-path that uses gRPC metadata and the header mapping for X-Org was missing in the fast-path shim. That explains why only certain flows (quick switch + prefetch) hit it.

maya: impact: low frequency visible glitch but sensitive: shows other org's row keys in UI briefly. We should treat as data exposure surface even if ephemeral.

jamal: remediation plan proposal:
- hotfix prefetch cache key to include orgId (zane)
- add validation in prefetch that request.orgId exists and return 400 if absent (defensive)
- purge memcached/redis keys matching `prefetch:*` for last 24h in prod as emergency rollback step (ops)
- patch gateway fast-path to copy X-Org into metadata (anika)
- add unit test and e2e that does rapid org switch repro (devex)

zane: small Redis command to purge keys by pattern (run carefully):
```bash
# run on replica and sync, then run on writers
redis-cli --scan --pattern "prefetch:*" | xargs -L100 redis-cli unlink
```

leo: +1. Also update rollout strategy: current canary targets host buckets. We need canaries that respect org isolation (i.e., don't roll new prefetch code to machines serving mixed-traffic orgs simultaneously). Otherwise we risk exposing buggy behavior across many orgs during rollout.

maya: agree — add a rollout note: "canary by org id or by tenant affinity when deploying fixes that affect scoping/caching" to the runbook.

sre-oncall: temporary mitigation applied: disabled aggressive prefetch feature-flag for prod at 2026-03-20T15:02:00Z to reduce incidence. Monitoring will alert on any flash > 100ms.

jamal: i'll open a PR for the cacheKey patch + defensive check. Can someone own the key purge and gateway shim?

anika: i'll own the gateway fast-path mapping.

zane: i'll do the cache patch and the e2e. ops/sre if you can schedule the key purge window (low traffic) and monitor.

deploy-bot: deploy request created by jamal for prefetch hotfix -> staging, CI passed.

maya: thanks team. after hotfix we should run a synthetic quick-switch test across 100 orgs to validate no cross-visibility.

jamal: noted — will include synthetic in the PR checklist.

sre-oncall: tracking ticket: PLAT-4823 (console-prefetch-namespace-race). I'm updating runbook and alerting docs now.

maya: leaving links: heap trace + repro gist -- https://redwood-internal/gh/repodumps/prefetch-repro 

zane: pushing patch to PR 4789. tagging @anika for gateway review.

leo: postmortem/notes required if we see >1 incident — flagging for next retro. :warning:
